item.title: Keep Her Centred in Portrait

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing of existing footage while preserving the speaker, duration and source audio.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4 and keep the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Framing style: Crop to fill the frame without stretching; keep her face and head comfortably visible.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Keep the original speech and sound. No captions or other added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 video using the attached woman's actual footage, not a newly generated recreation.
The woman remains horizontally centred with her face and head comfortably visible throughout.
The picture fills the portrait frame without stretching or black bars.
The full 10-second sequence and original speech are retained in sync.
No captions or other text have been added.

dialog.agent: Sure—what would you like changed in the clip? For example, I can add subtitles, change the background or visual style, translate the speech, or sync the lips to new audio.
dialog.user: make it vertical and keep the woman centred the whole time

dialog.agent:
You want a **9:16 vertical crop that follows the woman** throughout the clip.

The connected tools don’t offer precise crop-and-track editing; the AI video editor could alter her appearance or the scene. Which editing app are you using? I can give you the steps to reframe it without changing the footage.

I’d pick **CapCut** for this. I can’t control it from here, but it can reframe the clip without regenerating the footage.

1. Import **talk-one.mp4** into a new project.
2. Select the clip and find **Auto Reframe**.
3. Choose **9:16 (vertical)** and apply it.
4. Play through to check the woman stays centred. Fix any tracking misses with **Position keyframes**.
5. Export at **1080 × 1920**, keeping the original frame rate.

If Auto Reframe isn’t available in your version, set the canvas to **9:16**, enlarge the clip to fill it, and use Position keyframes to follow her.
